clue.text: Priest with a couple of Bishops, heading East

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, so two bishops give two Bs

indicators.note: heading here means the leading letter of the following word, East

explanation.surface: A clergyman travels eastward accompanied by two bishops.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbé is a French cleric, the title given to a priest in France.

clue.text: Gear engineers installed in alarm

indicators.note: installed in says the engineers letters are fitted inside the alarm word

parts.note: to appal is to dismay or alarm
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers fit equipment into an alarm system.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear in the sense of clothing or garments.

clue.text: Leaf caught in child's grip

indicators.note: in says the caught letter sits within the word for child

parts.note: a brat is a child, usually an unruly one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A leaf is clutched in a youngster's hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grip' completes the picture of the child's hold on the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A bract is a modified leaf growing at the base of a flower.

clue.text: A sign of love that's sweet

definitions.meaning: a gesture of affection given with the lips
a small confection, such as a meringue or chocolate drop of that name

explanation.surface: A loving gesture is described as sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an affectionate touch of the lips and a small confection or sweetmeat.

clue.text: Capital taken from African country lands in Western Europe

indicators.note: capital means the initial letter, and taken from says it is removed from the country name

parts.note: Liberia is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A capital city is captured from an African nation by forces landing in Western Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests a city such as Monrovia; here it is a capital letter, the initial L.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian peninsula comprises Spain and Portugal, the territory in Europe's south-west.

clue.text: Berkshire town's top journalist is discarded

parts.note: Slough is a town in Berkshire, an English county west of London
ED, editor, is the senior journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: A senior reporter from a Berkshire town is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Shed or cast off, as a snake does with its old skin.

clue.text: Pay tribute to a good person

parts.note: taken as written
ST, short for saint, is the crossword stock for a good person

explanation.surface: Someone honours a virtuous individual.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise glasses and drink to someone is a way of honouring them.

clue.text: Large cask writer provided after game in Kentish town

indicators.note: after says the writer comes behind the game in the answer

parts.note: a tun is a large barrel for wine or beer
bridge is a card game
H. G. Wells was the English author of The War of the Worlds

explanation.surface: A big barrel and an author turn up following a match in a Kent town.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a spa town in Kent, south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Tunbridge Wells is a spa town in the county of Kent.

clue.text: Decking put Navy crew in a spot

indicators.note: in says the navy and crew letters go within the other pair

parts.note: a dot is a spot
RN is the Royal Navy
men are the crew of a ship

explanation.surface: Sailors are put in a difficult position over the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decking' looks like a ship's deck; it means dressing up or decorating.
explanation.definitionFit: Decking in the sense of decorating or embellishing, as in decking the halls.

clue.text: Gifts of money once

definitions.meaning: an ancient unit of weight and currency in Greece and the Middle East

explanation.surface: Presents of cash given in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means natural aptitudes and also ancient units of money, as in the biblical parable.

clue.text: Act of worship with Holy Writ, perhaps, in admirable way

parts.note: praise is an act of worship

indicators.note: perhaps says the words beside it are an example to be reworked, not taken as they stand

explanation.surface: Worship accompanied by scripture is admirably conducted.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserving of commendation, done so as to merit approval.

clue.text: Get runs in match, that is plain

indicators.note: in says the runs letter is placed within the word for match

parts.note: a pair is a matching couple
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
IE, id est, is Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A cricketer scores runs in a game played on flat ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a wide grassy flatland, a plain in the noun sense.

clue.text: Have an ambition that helps the other side

parts.note: to own something is to have it
an ambition is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: An aspiration that ends up benefiting one's opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, putting the ball into your own net scores a point for the opposing team.

clue.text: Sort of wall that could be made in granite

indicators.note: could be made says the letters given can be reworked into something new

explanation.surface: A kind of wall that a builder might construct from granite.
explanation.definitionFit: A retaining wall holds back earth or water behind it on a slope.

clue.text: Arrested for quarrel

definitions.meaning: to be taken into custody by police, in an informal phrase
a heated argument or clash between people

explanation.surface: Someone was detained after a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means taken into custody; hyphenated as a noun it means a row or confrontation.

clue.text: Carrier? This ship's smaller

definitions.meaning: one who hauls or lugs heavy loads
a small sailing vessel with lugsails, smaller than many ships

explanation.surface: A boat used for transport is described as rather small.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is jocular: someone who lugs things. The second is the small two- or three-masted vessel rigged with lugsails.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person who hauls things and a small lug-rigged fishing boat.

clue.text: Information about long-established staff in plant

indicators.note: about says the information word goes round the long-established word

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
old means long-established
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Details about long-serving employees at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' and 'staff' suggest a workplace; plant is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow-flowered perennial herb of the daisy family.

clue.text: Irritates son, being redundant

parts.note: to needle someone is to irritate or provoke them

explanation.surface: A boy annoys others by being surplus to requirements.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unnecessary or superfluous is redundant.

clue.text: Reduce tameness of puzzle

definitions.meaning: split as two words, to become less tame

explanation.surface: To make something less docile is a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to confuse; split into two words it means to grow less tame.

clue.text: Extension of loan, say, with a lot of banknotes extra

parts.note: a roll is a wad of banknotes, as in a bankroll
over means in excess or left as extra

explanation.surface: A loan is lengthened, with a large wad of cash on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling a debt over defers repayment, extending its term; the hyphenated noun is the financial term.

clue.text: Allow in again to study with American college

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A student is readmitted to study at an American university.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit once more, letting someone enter a second time.

clue.text: Church worker coming from Essex to Norfolk

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A parish employee travels from one English county to another.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex and Norfolk are counties in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton looks after a church building and its graveyard, often digging graves.

clue.text: Lack of influence about, say, a bunch of flowers

indicators.note: about says the lack-of-influence phrase goes round the other piece

parts.note: having no say is lacking any influence
EG, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: Someone without power brings a bouquet.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'no say' goes round EG.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small posy of fragrant flowers.

clue.text: Dreadful score test opener got — a duck

indicators.note: dreadful says the letters are in a terrible mess
opener means the first letter of test

explanation.surface: A batsman scores a duck, out for nothing, in a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: SCORE plus T rearranges. Cricket misleads: a duck is zero runs, but here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoter is a dark sea duck.

clue.text: Miss a green — up in arms

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green, heraldry being the language of coats of arms

explanation.surface: Someone misses a putting green and becomes indignant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up in arms' looks like anger but signals heraldry, where colours have their own names.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert something is to turn it aside or avoid it, so to miss it.

clue.text: Amplifies how amusement shows on one's face

definitions.meaning: makes bigger or louder, a verb in the third person

definitions.text: how amusement shows on one's face
definitions.meaning: split as two words, a laughing face is in folds or wrinkles

explanation.surface: Something gets louder, as delight spreads across someone's features.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means makes larger; read as two words it describes a face wrinkled with laughter.

clue.text: Point lace

definitions.meaning: to add alcohol or drugs secretly to a drink

explanation.surface: A tip made of lace.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a sharp point and also to add liquor secretly to a drink.

clue.text: Injured grabbing one in second half for United

indicators.note: grabbing says the damaged word takes hold of the numeral inside it

parts.note: marred means spoiled or damaged
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A footballer is hurt seizing a chance in the second half for Manchester United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In second half' tells you where the one goes: into the back half of the word for injured. The football picture misleads; the definition is joined in wedlock.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedded couple are joined together, united in marriage.

clue.text: Powerful relation

definitions.meaning: having a strong, striking effect, as a forceful argument does
a recounting or narrating of a story

explanation.surface: A strong family connection.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means striking or effective, and also the act of recounting a story.

clue.text: Present of plaything a daughter held back

indicators.note: held says the toy word holds the other letters within it

parts.note: a toy is a plaything

indicators.note: back says the pair of letters are written backwards

explanation.surface: A girl's toy is kept back as a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns AD into DA, which sits inside TOY.
explanation.definitionFit: The present is this current day, the here and now.

clue.text: Well done? By no means uncommon

definitions.meaning: describing meat cooked very lightly, the opposite of thoroughly cooked

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether something was well done and is told it was unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes lightly cooked steak and also means scarce or unusual.

clue.text: Each one, except the first, is jolly

indicators.note: except the first says the opening letter is dropped from the word for each one

parts.note: every means each one of a group

explanation.surface: Everyone except the leader is cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like cheerful but is the British informal intensifier, as in 'jolly good'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage jolly is an adverb meaning extremely, as in jolly good.
